question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(7,-2,3)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨5,-1,6⟩)\cdot ⟨-6,3,2⟩=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(5,-1,6).$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨5,-1,6⟩-⟨7,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-6,3,2⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-2)\cdot (-6)+1\cdot 3+3\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|12+3+6|}{\sqrt{36+9+4}} \\  & =\frac{|21|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{21}{7} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
